summary:
Space Crisis is a 3D survival and resource-management game set on a barren, rocky world. In the game, players play as a stranded astronaut fighting to stay alive while repairing a damaged space base over a 30-day mission. Players explore the open terrain to collect useful supplies like wood, rocks, and spare parts from scattered crates while carefully watching their dropping oxygen levels and health. Using these gathered items, players must fix broken solar panels and build basic survival tools like campfires to keep the base running.

This project addresses the challenge of deep-space survival and limited resources in harsh environments. It is important because it turns complex space-exploration problems—like energy management, oxygen limits, and base repairs—into a fun, hands-on experience that teaches players how to plan ahead and solve problems under pressure.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Space Crisis is a browser-based 3D first-person survival and resource-management game set on a rocky, barren off-world outpost. Players step into the role of an astronaut on a 30-day mission to keep a damaged space habitat operational while managing limited life-support supplies.

  • Core Mechanics: Using standard first-person movement and interaction controls, players explore the desert-like terrain, scavenge scattered cargo crates and rock formations for raw materials (such as wood, rocks, and spare components), and store them in a 5-slot hotbar inventory.
  • Objectives & Survival: Players must balance depleting oxygen and health meters while completing critical base repairs—such as fixing damaged solar panels (pressing E near broken panels), constructing base towers, and assembling survival setups like campfires to endure the harsh environment.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Because it runs directly inside a standard web browser with no downloads, installations, or high-end gaming hardware required, anyone with an internet connection can play it immediately.
  • Active Problem-Solving: Rather than passively reading about space survival, players experience cause-and-effect decision-making—deciding whether to push farther out for materials or return to repair power systems before oxygen runs out.
  • Intuitive Gameplay Loop: Simple visual indicators (a 30-day counter, health/oxygen bars, task prompts, and a clear 5-slot inventory) make the mechanics easy to understand within seconds.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

The project aims to make the realities of deep-space exploration and off-world habitation engaging and easy to grasp for students and everyday players. By turning real astronaut challenges—energy generation via solar arrays, strict oxygen management, and salvaging limited materials—into an interactive 3D experience, Space Crisis encourages curiosity about space science, sustainability, and resourcefulness under pressure.

Tools, Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

(Note: Based on your video and links—adjust any specific engine or asset names if you used additional tools)

  • Game Engine & Web Deployment: Built for the web using GDevelop (gd.games) and deployed as a lightweight web application via Vercel (space-crisis.vercel.app).
  • Technologies & Languages: HTML5, JavaScript, and WebGL for 3D browser rendering, paired with event-based game logic and custom UI scripting.
  • 3D Assets & Design: 3D low-poly environmental models (terrain, boulders, supply crates, habitat modules, solar panels, and campfire props) combined with custom 2D HUD overlays.
  • Hardware: Developed and tested on standard consumer PC/laptop hardware running a modern Chromium-based web browser.

How Is the Project Creative?

Instead of a traditional 2D space shooter or text quiz, Space Crisis places the player directly inside a 3D planetary landscape where survival depends on maintenance and salvage rather than combat. Combining open-area scavenging, physical base repairs, and a multi-day survival countdown creates a grounded, atmospheric "stranded astronaut" experience right inside a web browser.

What Factors Did the Team Consider?

  • Performance & Accessibility: Keeping 3D geometry and textures lightweight so the game loads fast and runs smoothly in a web browser without lag.
  • Clarity of Objectives: Providing clear on-screen task counters (such as "DAY 1/30" and "Repair... 0/3 fixed") and interaction prompts (E to repair, R to retry) so players always know their immediate goal.
  • Pacing & Tension: Tuning oxygen depletion rates and the distance between the main habitat, solar arrays, and outlying supply crates so players feel urgency when exploring away from base.
